PortRules.Fix: Switch Telnet off in the device's settings. Use SSH or the device's app instead.
PortRules.Title: Telnet is switched on (unencrypted remote login)
PortRules.Why: Telnet sends passwords in plain text and is a common way in for attackers and botnets.

PortRules.Fix: Switch Telnet off in the device's settings. Use SSH or the device's app instead.
PortRules.Title: Telnet is switched on (unencrypted remote login)
PortRules.Why: Telnet sends passwords in plain text and is a common way in for attackers and botnets.

PortRules.Fix: Switch off developer options or ADB debugging on the device.
PortRules.Title: Android debugging is open (full control of the device)
PortRules.Why: Anyone on the network can install apps on the device and control it.

PortRules.Fix: Switch VNC off, or protect it with a strong password and allow only the computers that need it.
PortRules.Title: VNC remote screen is open
PortRules.Why: VNC often has a weak password or none, and gives control of the screen.

PortRules.Fix: Restrict Redis to the machine that uses it, and set a password.
PortRules.Title: Redis database is open
PortRules.Why: Redis usually has no password and can be used to take over the machine it runs on.

PortRules.Fix: Put the controller on its own network, or limit Modbus to the system that needs it.
PortRules.Title: Modbus industrial control is open
PortRules.Why: Modbus has no login: anyone on the network can read and change the controller's settings.

PortRules.Fix: Ask the internet provider whether it should be reachable here, and update the router.
PortRules.Title: Router management (TR-069) is open on the home network
PortRules.Why: This is the internet provider's remote management port. It has been used in large router attacks.

PortRules.Fix: Update the recorder, change its password, and keep it off the internet. Replace it if it is no longer updated.
PortRules.Title: Cheap DVR control port is open
PortRules.Why: This port belongs to low-cost recorders and cameras with a long record of security problems.

PortRules.Fix: Switch FTP off if nothing uses it, or use SFTP instead.
PortRules.Title: FTP is switched on (unencrypted file transfer)
PortRules.Why: FTP sends passwords and files in plain text.

PortRules.Fix: Switch it off if it isn't needed, and make sure the account has a strong password.
PortRules.Title: Remote Desktop is open
PortRules.Why: Remote Desktop is a common target for password guessing.

PortRules.Fix: Set a password on the MQTT broker, or limit it to the devices that use it.
PortRules.Title: MQTT messaging is open
PortRules.Why: MQTT without a password lets anyone on the network read or send smart-home messages.

PortRules.Fix: Update the camera or recorder firmware and change its password.
PortRules.Title: Dahua camera service port is open
PortRules.Why: Older Dahua firmware has had serious flaws on this port.

PortRules.Fix: Turn on authentication and use the encrypted console (41797) only.
PortRules.Title: Crestron console is reachable without encryption
PortRules.Why: The unencrypted console can be used to read or change the processor's settings.

PortRules.Fix: Check what is shared, and switch sharing off where it isn't needed.
PortRules.Title: Windows file sharing is open
PortRules.Why: Shared folders can expose files, and old versions of file sharing have been used by ransomware.

VersionRules.Fix: Update the device's firmware. If no update exists, replace it or keep it on a separate network.
VersionRules.Title: Very old SSH server
VersionRules.Why: This SSH version is many years old and has known security flaws.

VersionRules.Fix: Replace the device, or keep it on a separate network with no internet access.
VersionRules.Title: Windows CE is no longer updated
VersionRules.Why: Microsoft stopped security updates for Windows CE, so new flaws will never be fixed.
